# Two examples

We screened splice junctions in the 0, 1 and 6 hour libraries for changes
that occur in the same direction in all four donors. The two examples show
different kinds of transcript change: **CREM** has a strong internal-promoter
signal, while **TTLL7** shows a change consistent with skipping an annotated exon.
CREM has a documented activity-response role; TTLL7 has an experimentally
supported neuronal role, but its changing junction has not been functionally
validated in this stimulation experiment.

# CREM: an internal-promoter-associated junction

CREM has one clear changing junction: a junction from an internal exon to the common downstream exon
rises from **9/60 (15.0%)** of reads at that acceptor at baseline to
**270/414 (65.2%)** at 1 hour and **941/1,241 (75.8%)** at 6 hours.

CREM is an activity-responsive gene. An alternative intronic promoter is
known to produce the inducible CREM isoform ICER
([Molina et al., 1993](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8252624/)).
The observed junction starts beside an annotated internal CREM transcript
start, so **alternative promoter usage is a plausible explanation**. We
have not established that these particular molecules are ICER transcripts.
The figure shows a change in *junction usage*; it does not by itself prove
within-cell regulation by stimulation.

# The CREM sashimi plot

![CREM sashimi plot: pooled donor-assigned primary reads at 0, 1 and 6 hours. The short junction at the right has 9, 270 and 941 supporting reads, respectively; the 0 hour arc is below the display threshold.](assets/CREM_sashimi.png)

*CREM, chr10, plus strand. Each panel pools reads from CD_21, CD_31,
CD_36 and CD_48 at one timepoint. Colored areas show raw coverage. Curves
connect aligned segments across an intron; the number on a curve is its
supporting-read count. The black rows below are selected transcript models.
Arcs drawn above and below the coverage do not represent different directions
of change.*

The junction of interest is the **short, heavy curve on the right**,
connecting genomic positions **35,195,215–35,206,894**. It is labeled
**270** at 1 hr and **941** at 6 hr. It has **9** supporting reads at
0 hr, below this figure's arc display threshold. The plot also shows junctions elsewhere in the
gene. Neither the visible labels nor all the arcs in a panel form the
denominator for this event.

# CREM usage calculation

At this locus, several junctions end at the same **acceptor**,
chr10:35,206,894. For each timepoint we add the counts of *all* junctions
ending there, across the four donor-assigned cell sets. The usage rate is:

> **CREM internal-junction usage = reads on the 35,195,215–35,206,894
> junction ÷ reads on every junction ending at 35,206,894.**

| Time after stimulation | Target-junction reads | All junction reads at the acceptor | Target usage |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 hr | 9 | 60 | 15.0% |
| 1 hr | 270 | 414 | 65.2% |
| 6 hr | 941 | 1,241 | 75.8% |

For example, at 6 hr: **941 ÷ 1,241 = 0.758**, or **75.8%**. The
denominator includes rare alternatives not labeled on the sashimi plot.
These are fractions of *junction-supporting reads*, not measured fractions
of full-length CREM transcripts. Using fractions matters because total read
depth differs greatly among timepoints.

We checked each donor separately before pooling. The same junction gains
usage from 0 to 6 hr in **all four donors**:

| Donor | 0 hr | 6 hr |
|---|---:|---:|
| CD_21 | 5/23 (21.7%) | 274/371 (73.9%) |
| CD_31 | 0/12 (0%) | 305/388 (78.6%) |
| CD_36 | 0/10 (0%) | 141/199 (70.9%) |
| CD_48 | 4/15 (26.7%) | 221/283 (78.1%) |

The pooled percentages above give greater weight to donors with more reads.
The candidate screen instead averages the **four donor-specific changes**,
giving each donor equal weight; for this junction its mean change from 0 to
6 hr is **+0.633**, or **63.3 percentage points**.

# TTLL7: an exon-skipping pattern in a neuronal gene

TTLL7 modifies tubulin in neurons. Experimental depletion suppressed
nerve-growth-factor-stimulated neurite growth in PC12 cells and reduced
beta-tubulin polyglutamylation in primary neurons
([Ikegami et al., 2006](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16901895/)).
That supports a neuronal role for the **gene**, but does not establish that
this particular junction is regulated by stimulation or changes TTLL7 protein
function.

![TTLL7 sashimi plot at 0, 1 and 6 hours, pooling primary alignments from four donor-assigned cell sets at each timepoint. The short junction has 573, 1153 and 1066 reads; the competing long junction has 81, 336 and 1116 reads.](assets/TTLL7_sashimi.png)

*TTLL7, chr1, minus strand. Numbers on curves are supporting reads, not
percentages. The short arc is at the far left; the long arc reaches from the
left to the far right. Arc placement above or below the coverage has no
biological meaning. The black track is one GENCODE reference transcript.*

Both arcs end at the same TTLL7 exon boundary at **chr1:83,951,977**. The
short junction spans **83,951,977–83,952,186**, entering the intervening
annotated exon. The long junction spans **83,951,977–83,998,930** and
bypasses that 201-nucleotide exon. In the minus-strand transcript, this is
consistent with skipping the second exon of the displayed reference model.
We have not established complete isoforms or the protein consequence.

> **TTLL7 long-junction usage = reads on the 83,951,977–83,998,930
> junction ÷ reads on every junction starting at 83,951,977.**

| Time after stimulation | Short-junction reads | Long-junction reads | All junction reads at shared site | Long-junction usage |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 hr | 573 | 81 | 659 | 12.3% |
| 1 hr | 1,153 | 336 | 1,491 | 22.5% |
| 6 hr | 1,066 | 1,116 | 2,198 | 50.8% |

At 6 hr, **1,116 ÷ 2,198 = 50.8%**. The denominator includes 16 reads
on other rare junctions at this boundary, which is why it exceeds
1,066 + 1,116. The long-junction usage rises in **each of the four donors**:
from 7.3–16.0% at baseline to 46.8–57.1% at 6 hr. The mean of the four
donor-specific changes is **+39.8 percentage points**. As for CREM, these
are fractions of junction-supporting reads, not fractions of full-length
transcripts; changes in cell composition could also affect the pattern.

# How candidates were selected

The screen counts every `N` operation in the BAM alignment CIGAR as a
junction. It uses **primary alignments from donor-assigned cells** on
chromosomes 1–22, counted separately by donor and timepoint. Junctions are
compared when they share either genomic boundary; usage is calculated within
that shared-site group. An unobserved junction is assigned **zero usage**
only when that site has enough reads to evaluate it.

A candidate needs at least **10 reads at the site per donor at the shallower
timepoint** and **20 at the deeper timepoint**, a consistent direction of
change in all four donors, and an average change of at least **15 percentage
points**. The screen compares 0→1, 0→6 and 1→6 hr. Under these exploratory
rules it yielded **1,022 junction rows across 392 genes**. Rows may describe
competing junctions at the same site, so they are not 1,022 independent
splicing events.

CREM and TTLL7 were chosen because their junction shifts are large and
consistent across all four donors, and because their genes have documented
activity-responsive and neuronal roles, respectively. The two examples
illustrate different transcript structures.
The displayed counts were checked against donor-specific junction tables
and the filtered BAM inputs. The screen has no formal replicate-aware
test or multiple-testing correction, and the current analysis pools cell
types within each donor.

The complete [candidate gene table](assets/candidate_genes_v2.tsv) is
available for exploring other loci. BDNF is another strong
activity-responsive example, but its main change concerns alternative
first exons/promoters. The observed NRXN2 junction is a terminal-intron
event and should not be labeled as the classic neurexin SS4 event.

The relevant scripts are `7.sashimi/1.extract_junctions.sbatch` and
`7.sashimi/14.find_candidates_v2.R`. Counts and candidate tables are in
`long_read_processed/junctions/`. The plotted regional BAMs and the
`CREM_sashimi.png` source figure is in `7.sashimi/out/`; the TTLL7 source
figure and donor-level usage table are in `7.sashimi/out/ttll7_review/`.
